subject: Retention alignment and temporary purge pause request — HealthSync Labs
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@healthsynclabs.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@patel-law.com, ops@backup-thirdparty.io
Date: 2028-03-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary retention extension request + purge pause for upcoming audit

Hi Priya,

Hope you're well — we have an upcoming compliance audit in the EU the week of Mar 13 and the auditor is insisting on access to historical backups going back 12 months for a targeted dataset (patient match logs for onboarding flows). Our normal contracted retention is 90 days for snapshots and 180 days for logs, which won't satisfy them.

Can Redwood temporarily extend snapshot retention for the HealthSync account so the specific snapshots are preserved until 2028-04-30, and pause the scheduled backup purge planned for Mar 17? We'll sign a narrow addendum. We only need the retention for the dataset tagged HSL-onboard-evt and related logs; nothing else.

We attach the auditor's request and our legal team's draft (HealthSync_DPA_redline_v3.pdf). Please let me know the operational constraints and any evidence you can provide post-purge (deletion certificates).

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Li
Head of Compliance, HealthSync Labs

Subject: Fwd: Temporary retention extension request + purge pause for upcoming audit

Team — forwarding HealthSync's ask. Key asks: pause purge on 2028-03-17, extend snapshots for tag HSL-onboard-evt until 2028-04-30, and provide deletion confirmation afterwards. They will sign a short addendum but want limited-scope retention.

Operational questions I need answered before I reply to Emma:
- Can we implement a targeted retention extension by tag without affecting global purge windows?
- What are the audit/evidence artifacts we can produce (snapshot manifest, object-level deletion log, signed deletion affidavit)?
- Any subprocessor concerns for backups stored with our third-party object-store in eu-west-1? HealthSync flagged cross-border risk and wants assurance about subprocessors.

I'm attaching a proposed matrix of affected snapshots to use as the canonical list we can preserve (backup-snapshot-matrix.csv). Please review and respond with a proposed timeline and any legal gating items.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@patel-law.com, security@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-04T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention extension request + purge pause for upcoming audit

Priya / Marissa — quick legal note and redline guidance:

1) Scope and duration: we should accept a narrowly scoped retention addendum limited to the explicit tags and snapshot IDs HealthSync provides. Add a fixed expiry (2028-04-30) after which standard purge resumes and we will run a deletion confirmation.

2) Subprocessors & data location: HealthSync is right to ask for subprocessor confirmation. We must provide the active subprocessor list (object-store provider, backup indexing service, and encryption KMS) and a statement that no cross-border transfer will be initiated beyond eu-west-1 for these preserved snapshots. If any cross-border subprocessors exist, require prior written consent.

3) Technical safeguards: require that preserved snapshots remain encrypted under our CMK (customer-managed KMS) or our documented equivalent, and that access is strictly limited to Redwood personnel on the access-control list.

4) Deletion evidence: propose a two-step proof — (a) runbook output listing object keys scheduled for deletion, (b) post-deletion manifest with SHA256 hashes and a signed certificate from Redwood security. We should avoid language that creates a long-term escrow obligation.

5) Fee & change control: propose a one-time operational fee and an addendum executed via DocuSign.

I can draft the addendum language for the DPA redline they sent (short, scoped amendment). Legal needs the final snapshot list and confirmation from Ops that the targeted extension is implementable without risking other customers.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@backup-thirdparty.io
Date: 2028-03-05T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention extension request + purge pause for upcoming audit

Priya / team — operational plan from Ops:

Summary: We can implement a targeted retention extension by tag. High-level steps:
1) Ingest HealthSync's canonical list (backup-snapshot-matrix.csv) and mark the listed snapshot objects with a preservation flag in our metadata store. Flags expire at 2028-04-30T23:59:59Z.
2) Pause automated purge job for any object with preservation flag (we will scope the pause to the account + tag to avoid wider schedule changes). Purge job runs are idempotent and can skip preserved objects.
3) Run a dry-run list on 2028-03-17 to confirm preserved objects would otherwise have been deleted, create manifest (object key, size, sha256).
4) After 2028-04-30, run a final deletion job for preserved objects with a before/after manifest and provide a signed deletion certificate.

Constraints / notes:
- Third-party object-store (provider: eu-storage-nv) will retain copies for up to 14 additional days in their internal lifecycle; we will request immediate object-level deletion but cannot control their internal replication windows. We'll request ops@backup-thirdparty.io to confirm their deletion TTL and provide evidence.
- KMS: We will keep objects encrypted under Redwood-managed key scoped to eu-west-1 unless HealthSync provides a CMK ARN. If they require CMK, we need it by Mar 10.
- Timeline: we can implement the preservation flags by Mar 10 (assuming final snapshot list by Mar 07). Dry-run on Mar 17 as requested. Final deletion run during maintenance window after Apr 30 (propose May 02 to allow extra verification).

Attachments: ops-purge-runbook-draft.md (contains commands and manifest template). I'll coordinate with the third-party ops team for deletion evidence.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: ops-purge-runbook-draft.md

Subject: Re: Retention alignment and temporary purge pause request — HealthSync Labs

Emma — thanks for the detailed request and redline. Summary and proposed plan below; please confirm so we can proceed with the addendum.

What Redwood will do (targeted, limited-scope):
- Preserve the set of snapshot objects you provide (tag HSL-onboard-evt) by applying a preservation flag. Preservation expires 2028-04-30T23:59:59Z.
- Pause our automated purge for objects with the preservation flag (this is account+tag scoped). Dry-run manifest will be delivered on 2028-03-17.
- Final deletion run will occur during the May 02 maintenance window; Redwood will deliver pre-/post-deletion manifests and a signed deletion certificate within 5 business days of completion.
- No cross-border transfer will be initiated; stored copies will remain in eu-west-1. We will provide our active subprocessor list and SOC2 evidence for the object-store and indexing service prior to executing the preservation.
- If you require use of your CMK, please provide the ARN by 2028-03-10; otherwise objects will remain under Redwood-managed EU CMK.
- One-time operational fee: EUR 3,200 (covers manual runbook validation and evidence package).

Next steps we need from HealthSync by 2028-03-07:
1) Final snapshot list (IDs and tags) — we'll use backup-snapshot-matrix.csv as the canonical list.
2) Confirmation on KMS preference (provide CMK ARN or accept Redwood-managed).
3) Sign the scoped DPA addendum (we will send via DocuSign once Legal finalizes language).

Kimberly will circulate the addendum redline; Aditya will coordinate the dry-run and final deletion manifests with ops@backup-thirdparty.io. Once you confirm, I'll generate the DocuSign link and route the agreement to your legal team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
